title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: these 1981-82 notes on 'déploiement' (unfolding) of stratified spaces. A stratified space of type I (I a finite poset) is to be rebuilt from 'unfolded' data. The data are: unfolded strata Σ_i, presumably manifolds with boundary/corners; for i<j, spaces Σ_ij with a fibration Σ_ij→Σ_i and a boundary map Σ_ij→Σ_j; and, for i<j<k, composition maps Σ_ij×_{Σ_j}Σ_jk→Σ_ik. Geometrically Σ_ij is the bundle of links of stratum i inside stratum j, embedded as part of the boundary of the unfolded j-th stratum. On the previous page Grothendieck indexes everything by flags d of I: Σ_d with transition maps, plus a cartesian condition (3), Σ_{d∪d'} = Σ_d ×_{Σ_i} Σ_{d'} when the last element of d is the first of d'. This page repackages that data categorically.
(1) A family (Σ_i)_{i∈I} is the same as one space Σ_* = ⊔Σ_i with a 'partition of type I', i.e. a continuous map Σ_* → I_M, where I_M is I as a discrete (constant) space.
(2) A family (Σ_ij)_{i≤j} is the same as one space Σ_** over Drap_1(I) ⊂ I×I. The convention is Σ_ij = ∅ unless i≤j, and Σ_ii = Σ_i.
(3) The maps Σ_ij→Σ_j and Σ_ij→Σ_i together are two maps b ('but', target) and s ('source'), from Σ_** to Σ_*. They are compatible with pr_2 and pr_1 from I×I to I, and the bipartition of Σ_** is recovered from that of Σ_* via (s,b). Here b is locally a closed map (an immersion) and s is a fibration.
(4) There is an 'identity morphism' i: Σ_* → Σ_** (the inclusion of the Σ_ii) with s∘i = b∘i = id.
(5) The page breaks off as the composition data Σ_ijk = Σ_ij ×_{Σ_j} Σ_jk → Σ_ik is about to be encoded. The next page completes it: an associative, unital composition, so Σ_** ⇉ Σ_* is a category object internal to spaces (an 'enriched category') over the poset I seen as a category.
Its nerve in degree n is ⊔ Σ_{i0…in} over flags of length n. The cartesian condition (3) of the previous page is exactly the Segal condition saying that Σ_• is the nerve of this internal category. So the page reduces the combinatorics of the flag-indexed system Σ_d to a topological category Σ_** ⇉ Σ_* fibred over I, with source a fibration and target a boundary immersion. Grothendieck then uses this to construct the stratified space by gluing.
errors: Writing Σ_* ⊂ M is loose. The Σ_i here are the unfolded strata, which do not sit inside the stratified space M as disjoint subsets. Presumably Σ_* is meant as an abstract space, or M is a working notation.
The convention should read Σ_ij = ∅ unless i ≤ j, since Σ_ii = Σ_i is non-empty. 'si i ≮ j' is a slip, or a misreading of ≰.

The page makes no claim about b being injective globally. 'loc.t un morphisme fermé (i.e. une immersion)' only asserts a local closed immersion; injectivity on overlaps is handled by the conditions a)–c) in the previous page's margin.

ideas.what: Encoding an I-indexed family of spaces as a single space with a map to the discrete poset I ('partition of type I'); pairs as a space over Drap_1(I) ⊂ I×I.
ideas.modern_name: spaces fibred over a poset / stratified spaces as maps to a poset (Lurie HA App. A, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; made systematic by Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A, 2017) and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)

ideas.what: The unfolded data (strata Σ_i, link bundles Σ_ij → Σ_i that are boundary pieces of Σ_j, compositions Σ_ij×_{Σ_j}Σ_jk → Σ_ik) organized as an internal category Σ_** ⇉ Σ_* over the poset I, with source a fibration, target a boundary immersion, and an identity section.
ideas.modern_name: iterated fibration structure / resolution of Thom–Mather stratified spaces by manifolds with fibred corners; the unzip together with its link maps as a category object; Segal-type nerve over Drap(I)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom–Mather control data (1969–70); Verona, 'décollement' (LNM 1102, 1984); Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka 'unzip' (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5-6 on 'géométrie modérée' and the 'déploiement' of stratified spaces, describes the unfolding idea informally; I am unsure it uses the internal-category formulation.

ideas.what: Cartesian condition on flag-indexed Σ_d (from the previous page) identified with the existence of an associative composition, i.e. the nerve condition.
ideas.modern_name: Segal condition for the nerve of an internal category
ideas.where_published: Nerve characterization of categories: Grothendieck, FGA/Séminaire Bourbaki 'Techniques de construction…' (1960-61)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly formulates the unfolded (resolved) data of a stratified space as a topological category Σ_** ⇉ Σ_* fibred over the poset I. Its source map is a fibration (link bundles), its target map a boundary immersion, and the flag-indexed system Σ_d is its nerve. This links Thom–Mather/Verona-style resolution of stratified spaces to internal-category/Segal language. The later literature reached that language independently: manifolds with fibred corners (ALMP) and the unzip plus exit-path ∞-categories (Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Lurie).
missed.quote: deux morphismes "source" et "but" Σ_** →b Σ_*, s↓ Σ_* compatibles avec les pr_1 et pr_2 de I×I dans I … ici b est loc.t un morphisme fermé (i.e. est une immersion) et s est une fibration. On a de plus i : Σ_* → Σ_** "morphisme identité"
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is an early (1981-82) explicit categorical reconstruction datum for stratified spaces, predating Verona's décollement and AFT's unzip. A direct statement that a stratified space with conical structure is equivalent to such an internal category over I (with fibration/immersion conditions) might be worth comparing with AFT's reconstruction results. Credit-wise it is mostly of historical interest.

deep.surprise_reason: The categorical repackaging (internal category over I, nerve over flags) is clean and early. But the underlying geometry (control data, link bundles, unfolding into manifolds with corners) is classical. The 'déploiement' programme is announced in Esquisse d'un programme. Later work (Verona, ALMP, AFT) reached equivalent structures, so this is a notable early formulation rather than a missing result.
transcription_corrections: 'au dessus de I×J' should be 'au dessus de I×I'. The inserted word reads 'Drap_1(I)' (flags of length ≤1), not 'Drap[?] (I)'.
'Celle des Σ_j [-équivaut-] équivaut' should read 'Celle des Σ_ij équivaut'.
'Σ_{i,j} = ∅ si i ≮ j' is logically 'si i ≰ j', given Σ_ii = Σ_i.
'Comme la bipartition de type I de Σ_** est déduite de la partition de type I de Σ_*, et de b et s)' is the content of a parenthesis opened at '(NB' — the struck 'NB la ...'.
